answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks with quadratic staking: to vote, an agent locks a bond, and splitting it across fake identities is priced by the square of each part. Ten units in one hand buy ten votes, but ten shards need a hundred units of collateral for the same weight, so cost grows with every added identity. Like a harbor charging per berth or a prism splitting one beam into weak rays, extra bodies dilute influence rather than amplify it, and a cedar-sized treasury buys little power. Double-voting slashes the bonds, so the attack is costly and self-defeating.
